title: MERIDIAN FORGE men's accessories capsule: neutralize an 8-piece mixed-light jewelry batch to an in-frame grey card, vectorize the pendant spec sketch, author a plated colorway variant, and merge one review sheet per SKU
grounding_note: Adapted from a real Upwork men's-accessories brief (a U.S. men's jewelry label building a new pendant + chain line, working from 'detailed 2D illustrator sketches', wanting 'clean, factory-ready' files for its manufacturing partners plus catalog material for the design team's 'refinements and iterations' review loop; the poster also asked for 3D CAD work). The client is laundered to a FICTIONAL men's stainless-steel accessories house, MERIDIAN FORGE; no real company, product, person, or trademark is named. REPOSITIONED for connector reality: the brief's literal 3D-CAD-in-Rhino/Matrix core is firmly out of Adobe-connector scope (no 3D/CAD), so this task takes the faithful, Adobe-doable slice of the SAME engagement and SCALES it from the original single-pendant hero to the real workload: the maker photographed the whole eight-piece launch capsule (pendants, a chain, a signet ring, a cuff, cufflinks) as flat-lays on one seamless light-grey studio sweep, shot over two sessions under mismatched shop light (cool fluorescents, warm tungsten, a green shop-fixture, mixed window+tungsten, some under/over-exposed), and — because the light was inconsistent and the whole set has to read as one catalog — laid a photographic 18% neutral grey reference card into the corner of every frame. The Adobe chain does the honest work the brief rewards: neutralize every piece to its in-frame grey card so the set shares one white point while each stainless piece holds a true neutral-steel look and each plated piece keeps its genuine colorway; author a restrained brushed-steel house look from primitives; turn the industrial designer's flat 2D technical pendant sketch into a clean factory-ready vector; produce a seasonal plated colorway variant of one pendant without a re-plate or reshoot; then run the capsule through the client's authored single-record InDesign review-sheet template as a one-file-per-row data-merge so the design team gets one press-ready sheet per SKU. The eight-piece count, the two-session lighting split, the in-frame grey card, the studio sweep, the per-piece casts, the seasonal-variant ask, and the review-sheet endpoint are reasonable enrichment; nothing contradicts the source (men's pendant + chain line, stainless / plated production, factory-ready 2D asset, design-team review loop are all from the brief). No 3D/CAD, no generative fill, no compositing, no from-scratch layout is claimed.
one_line_ask: Take eight MERIDIAN FORGE capsule pieces photographed across two mismatched lighting sessions (each with a grey reference card in frame), neutralize every frame to the card so the set reads as one white point while each stainless piece stays true neutral steel and each plated piece keeps its genuine colorway, isolate every piece onto one shared clean catalog ground, turn the flat 2D pendant technical sketch into clean factory-ready vector, author a seasonal plated-colorway variant of one pendant, and merge one press-ready review sheet per SKU for the design team.
full_brief:
MERIDIAN FORGE is a small men's stainless-steel accessories label launching an eight-piece capsule, and we work off our industrial designer's flat 2D technical sketches. We are NOT asking for 3D or CAD here and we do NOT need the catalog laid out by hand — our design team runs the review. We need a retoucher and vector-prep specialist to turn a folder of raw sample photos and one technical drawing into a clean, coordinated set the team can sign off during our refinements-and-iterations loop.

What you're given: eight photographs, one per piece in the launch capsule (pendants, a box-link chain, a signet ring, a cuff bracelet, cufflinks), all laid out on the same seamless light-grey studio sweep. They were shot over two mornings under whatever bench light was on, so out of the folder they are a mismatched jumble — some cold and bluish, some warm and orange, one under a greenish shop fixture, a couple under/over-exposed. Because the light was a mess and the whole capsule has to look like one line, we dropped a photographic 18% neutral grey reference card into the corner of every frame. You are also given one flat 2D technical line drawing of our lead compass pendant (a raster export of the designer's Illustrator sketch), the client's InDesign review-sheet template, and a SKU roster.

The photo job (this is the core): make the eight pieces read as ONE catalog. Neutralize each frame to the grey card it carries — the card must read a clean neutral grey (no residual warm, cool, or green cast) and, once every card is neutral, the whole set must sit at one shared white point and brightness. Do NOT force one blanket correction across the batch: each frame was lit differently and needs its own white-balance, tint, and exposure decision to land on that shared target, and you must tell us the final move you made on each frame so we can confirm the set was matched, not eyeballed. Be careful with true colour: most of these pieces are bare stainless and must end as clean neutral steel, but at least one is a warm-toned plated piece whose real colour is the point — judge every piece on the card in its own frame, and do not cool a genuinely warm plated metal chasing a steel-grey neutral it was never meant to have. Carry one restrained house look across the whole set — a premium brushed-steel tone that keeps the metal's grain and holds its highlights so nothing clips to blown white. Then lift every piece cleanly off the sweep onto one shared solid catalog ground so the eight packshots sit together as a coordinated set, with the metal edges clean and no messy halo; keep the reference card out of the delivered packshots. The pieces have real interior gaps (a pendant's bail loop, the chain's links, the ring's centre) — those must not be bricked in with solid colour; keep them reading as clean ground.

Second, a colourway variant with no reshoot and no re-plate: on the rose-gold pendant, give us a seasonal deepened 'antique bronze' version of the same shot — a richer, darker, slightly muted tone in the SAME warm metal family, not a jump to a far-off colour — and it has to sit under the real folds, brushed grain, highlights and shadow of the piece, touching only the pendant and never the ground.

Third, the technical drawing: turn the flat 2D pendant sketch into clean, razor-sharp vector art for the factory spec — it must scale to any size without looking like a fuzzy scan, and it must come from the drawing, not from a photo of the finished piece.

Finally, build the review set: we have hand-built the InDesign review-sheet template with the real placeholder fields and a product-image slot, and we're giving you the roster; merge them so every SKU gets its own single-page sheet with its name, code, material, finish and notes set in type and its matching cleaned packshot dropped in, then hand back one press-ready ~300 DPI US Letter PDF covering every SKU, one page per piece. Bind the copy verbatim from the roster — do not rewrite it. Acceptance: every grey card neutral and the whole set matched to one white point with the per-frame moves reported; each stainless piece true neutral steel and the plated pieces true to their real colour; every piece cleanly isolated on the shared ground with interior gaps intact; the antique-bronze variant natural under the existing light; the sketch a crisp vector; and exactly one finished sheet per roster row.

inputs.name: MF01_compass_pendant_flatlay.jpg
inputs.gen_prompt: Photoreal top-down product flat-lay of a single brushed stainless-steel men's compass pendant, rounded-square, roughly 30mm, with a soldered top bail loop and a finely engraved compass-rose motif on the face, laid flat on a seamless light-grey studio paper sweep. A photographic 18% neutral grey reference card sits flat on the sweep in the lower-left corner of the frame, clearly visible and uncropped. Shot under COOL bluish fluorescent bench light with a distinct blue-cyan cast, flat-to-normal contrast, and the whole frame tilted about 4 degrees clockwise. Real brushed-steel grain, faint micro-scratches, a soft contact shadow. Full-frame camera capture, about 4200x4200 px, straight off the camera, un-graded, documentary, not CGI-glossy. No text.
inputs.realism_notes: SKU MF-01, Session A (cool/blue), tilted ~4deg. The lead pendant; its bail loop is an enclosed interior gap. The in-frame 18% grey card is the neutralization target and its cool cast needs a warming temperature move OPPOSITE to the warm-session frames — a single shared white balance across the batch cannot serve both, which is the identical-params trap. Shot on the SAME light-grey sweep as the whole capsule so that after the knockout the enclosed bail-loop interior (which retains sweep pixels — image_remove_background isolates the outer background only and cannot punch an enclosed hole) reads as the shared catalog ground rather than a filled patch. The finished piece in this photo is NOT the vector source — the flat technical drawing (separate input) is; this is a photograph to be graded and isolated. Camera-scale ~4200px so the packshot fills the review-sheet image frame at >=300 DPI by downscale only.

inputs.name: MF02_box_link_chain_flatlay.jpg
inputs.gen_prompt: Photoreal top-down product flat-lay of a men's stainless-steel box-link chain, about 4mm wide, laid in a loose S-curve on a seamless light-grey studio paper sweep. A photographic 18% neutral grey reference card sits flat on the sweep at the frame edge, clearly visible and uncropped. Shot under WARM tungsten bench light with a strong orange cast, level, slightly bright. Real brushed-steel link facets, tiny micro-scratches, faint dust, a soft contact shadow. Full-frame camera capture, about 4200x4200 px, straight off the camera, un-graded, documentary, not CGI-glossy. No text.
inputs.realism_notes: SKU MF-02, Session B (warm/orange), level. The chain is dense with ENCLOSED link holes; because it is shot on the shared light-grey sweep, those interiors retain sweep pixels that read as the catalog ground after the outer-background knockout (the tool cannot punch enclosed holes, so a dark or mismatched ground would show captured sweep inside every link — the sweep=ground choice is what makes this survivable). Its warm cast needs a COOLING move — the opposite sign to the cool-session frames — so the whole set can share one white point. Grey card is the target.

inputs.name: MF03_signet_ring_flatlay.jpg
inputs.gen_prompt: Photoreal top-down product flat-lay of a men's brushed stainless-steel signet ring, plain shield face, laid on a seamless light-grey studio paper sweep, the band's open centre visible. A photographic 18% neutral grey reference card sits flat on the sweep at the frame edge, clearly visible and uncropped. Shot under near-neutral bench light with only a faint cast, slightly UNDER-exposed and flat, and the frame tilted about 3 degrees. Real brushed-steel grain and soft contact shadow. Full-frame camera capture, about 4200x4200 px, straight off the camera, un-graded, documentary, not CGI-glossy. No text.
inputs.realism_notes: SKU MF-03, Session A-ish (near-neutral but under-exposed), tilted ~3deg. Its grey card is close to neutral, so the dominant move is tonal (lift exposure to the shared brightness, hold the black point) with only a small white-balance nudge — over-warming or over-cooling it would push it off the matched set. The ring's centre is an enclosed hole covered by the sweep=ground choice.

inputs.name: MF04_rosegold_meridian_pendant_flatlay.jpg
inputs.gen_prompt: Photoreal top-down product flat-lay of a men's rose-gold PVD-plated pendant, a rounded vertical bar with a top bail loop, genuinely warm rose-gold in colour, laid on a seamless light-grey studio paper sweep. A photographic 18% neutral grey reference card sits flat on the sweep at the frame edge, clearly visible and uncropped. Shot under near-neutral daylight-balanced bench light so the grey card already reads neutral and the warm rose-gold colour is the real finish of the piece, not a lighting cast. Normal exposure, real plated sheen and faint brushed grain, soft contact shadow. Full-frame camera capture, about 4200x4200 px, straight off the camera, un-graded, documentary, not CGI-glossy. No text.
inputs.realism_notes: SKU MF-04, near-neutral light. THE TRAP FRAME and the source of the seasonal variant. Its warmth is the genuine rose-gold plating and its in-frame grey card ALREADY reads neutral, so the correct white-balance move is essentially NONE (only match exposure/brightness to the set) — an agent that batch-applies the cooling move used on the warm-session frames, or 'corrects an imagined warm cast', will drive the card off-neutral and strip the real plating colour the client is selling. The decision must be read from THIS card, not the batch. Separately, this same graded frame is the base for the authored 'antique bronze' colourway variant (a within-family deepen-and-mute, NOT a hue jump). Its bail loop is an enclosed gap covered by the sweep=ground choice.

inputs.name: MF05_cuff_bracelet_flatlay.jpg
inputs.gen_prompt: Photoreal top-down product flat-lay of a men's brushed stainless-steel open cuff bracelet, a smooth curved band with a gap, laid on a seamless light-grey studio paper sweep. A photographic 18% neutral grey reference card sits flat on the sweep at the frame edge, clearly visible and uncropped. Shot under old GREEN overhead shop-fixture fluorescent light with a distinct green/magenta-deficient cast, normal exposure, slightly dull. Real brushed-steel grain and soft contact shadow. Full-frame camera capture, about 4200x4200 px, straight off the camera, un-graded, documentary, not CGI-glossy. No text.
inputs.realism_notes: SKU MF-05, Session B (green fluorescent), level. The green cast needs a TINT correction (green->magenta), a different axis than the warm/cool temperature frames, so a temperature-only fix leaves the card green and fails the shared-white-point target. The cuff's inner curve is an open gap, not fully enclosed.

inputs.name: MF06_cufflinks_pair_flatlay.jpg
inputs.gen_prompt: Photoreal top-down product flat-lay of a pair of men's polished stainless-steel cufflinks with round faces, laid side by side on a seamless light-grey studio paper sweep. A photographic 18% neutral grey reference card sits flat on the sweep at the frame edge, clearly visible and uncropped. Shot under a MIX of cool window light on one side and warm tungsten on the other so the cast is split and uneven across the pair, normal exposure, flat contrast. Real polished-steel reflections and soft contact shadows. Full-frame camera capture, about 4200x4200 px, straight off the camera, un-graded, documentary, not CGI-glossy. No text.
inputs.realism_notes: SKU MF-06, Session mixed (split window+tungsten), level. The split cast is the hardest to neutralize: the agent must balance temperature and tint toward the card's neutral, accepting a compromise since the two sides disagree, rather than fully killing one side. A two-object frame, so the isolation spans both cufflinks.

inputs.name: MF07_onyx_anodized_pendant_flatlay.jpg
inputs.gen_prompt: Photoreal top-down product flat-lay of a men's black-anodized stainless-steel pendant, a matte dark dog-tag-style rectangle with a top bail loop, laid on a seamless light-grey studio paper sweep. A photographic 18% neutral grey reference card sits flat on the sweep at the frame edge, clearly visible and uncropped. Shot under COOL bench light, flat and clearly UNDER-exposed so the dark anodized surface muddies toward black. Real matte-anodized micro-texture and soft contact shadow. Full-frame camera capture, about 4200x4200 px, straight off the camera, un-graded, documentary, not CGI-glossy. No text.
inputs.realism_notes: SKU MF-07, Session A (cool, dark/under-exposed), level. Black-point discipline: warm to neutralize the card and LIFT exposure to the set brightness while holding the black point so the anodized surface stays a deep true black, neither crushed to pure 0 nor washed to grey. Its dark edge cuts cleanly against the light sweep, an easy isolation — the opposite difficulty to the near-tone pieces. Bail loop enclosed, covered by sweep=ground.

inputs.name: MF08_dogtag_compass_pendant_flatlay.jpg
inputs.gen_prompt: Photoreal top-down product flat-lay of a men's brushed stainless-steel dog-tag pendant, a rounded rectangle with a top bail loop, its face bearing a finely engraved compass-rose motif that at a glance resembles line art, laid on a seamless light-grey studio paper sweep. A photographic 18% neutral grey reference card sits flat on the sweep at the frame edge, clearly visible and uncropped. Shot under near-neutral bench light with a faint cast, level, normal exposure. Real brushed-steel grain, subtle engraving depth and micro-shadow, soft contact shadow. Full-frame camera capture, about 4200x4200 px, straight off the camera, un-graded, documentary, not CGI-glossy. No text.
inputs.realism_notes: SKU MF-08, near-neutral light, level. THE TRIAGE TRAP: this is a PHOTOGRAPH of a finished metal piece whose engraved compass-rose face superficially resembles the flat 2D technical drawing, so a naive agent may route it to vectorize (which, fed a photograph, returns a muddy black silhouette, not a spec) or skip its grade. The correct treatment is the same photo pipeline as the other pieces — neutralize to its card and isolate onto the shared ground; ONLY the flat raster sketch is vectorized. Getting the routing wrong is invisible until the file is inspected. Bail loop enclosed, covered by sweep=ground.

inputs.name: compass_pendant_technical_sketch.png
inputs.gen_prompt: A flat 2D technical line-art drawing of a men's compass pendant, front elevation: a rounded-square pendant roughly 30mm tall with a soldered top bail loop, clean black ink outlines on white, fine interior engraving lines suggesting a compass-rose motif, thin dimension tick marks at the edges. Rendered as a slightly low-contrast flatbed scan export to PNG: faint paper grain, the whole drawing rotated about 4 degrees clockwise, extra white margin around it, anti-aliased (not razor-crisp) ink edges. Pure black-on-white draftsman line work, no colour, no shading, no 3D.
inputs.realism_notes: The industrial designer's flat 2D sketch and the ONLY vector source. It is a raster export of a scanned/illustrated line drawing, not clean vector: visible ~4deg rotation, faint paper grain, soft anti-aliased edges, extra margin, so straighten + crop-to-bounds are genuine prep-before-trace work before image_vectorize produces a crisp factory SVG. Distinct in medium from the eight photographs (flat line art vs photographed metal), which is the triage the agent must resolve — this raster is traced; the photographed pieces, including the engraved dog-tag MF-08 that looks similar, are graded and isolated, never traced.

inputs.name: meridian_reviewsheet_template.indd
inputs.gen_prompt: AUTHORED DELIVERABLE (cannot be model-generated): a genuine, hand-built Adobe InDesign document (.indd/.idml) for a SINGLE-RECORD US Letter (8.5x11) portrait product review sheet, ONE piece per page. It must contain live InDesign data-merge placeholder fields <<product_name>>, <<sku>>, <<material>>, <<finish>>, <<review_notes>>, and ONE @-prefixed image-path merge column @packshot wired to a product-image frame (the matching cleaned packshot). Built by hand in InDesign so the merge fields and the image field actually bind. Explicitly NOT a convert_pdf_to_indd output and NOT a multi-record grid: document_merge_data_layout emits one file per row, so the template holds exactly one record's worth of fields; a converted-PDF template or a multi-up grid would not bind / cannot be produced.
inputs.realism_notes: document_merge_data_layout REQUIRES a user-authored .indd carrying real merge fields plus a genuine @image-path column, and it produces ONE FILE PER ROW — so a single-record review sheet is the correct, connector-doable shape (a multi-product grid catalog is impossible on this tool). Supplied as an input, not a chain output; a PDF-converted .indd with literal typed text would not bind. The @packshot column resolves each row to that SKU's agent-produced isolated packshot, so the eight graded photos have a real, connector-legal path onto the sheets without any free-form image-at-coordinates placement (which is banned).

inputs.name: meridian_capsule_roster.csv
inputs.gen_prompt: Generate a CSV with columns product_name,sku,material,finish,review_notes,@packshot holding 8 rows, one per capsule piece: Compass Pendant (MF-01), Box-Link Chain (MF-02), Signet Ring (MF-03), Meridian Rose-Gold Pendant (MF-04), Open Cuff Bracelet (MF-05), Round Cufflinks (MF-06), Onyx Anodized Pendant (MF-07), Dog-Tag Compass Pendant (MF-08). Each row carries the product name, its SKU code (e.g. MF-01), a material string (e.g. '316L stainless steel', 'Rose-gold PVD-plated steel', 'Black-anodized steel'), a finish string (e.g. 'Brushed', 'Polished', 'Matte anodized'), and a short one-to-two-line internal review note for the design team. The @packshot column names the matching cleaned packshot file (e.g. @mf01_packshot.png) so the one-file-per-row merge drops each isolated photo into that row's single-record sheet. Column names must exactly match the template merge fields <<product_name>>,<<sku>>,<<material>>,<<finish>>,<<review_notes>> and the @packshot image column.
inputs.realism_notes: Header names match the authored .indd fields and the @packshot image column so the one-file-per-row merge binds copy and the correct isolated photo per SKU. Eight rows fixes the page-count = row-count = 8 acceptance gate. Text-only merge (document_merge_data_vector) is explicitly the WRONG tool here because it cannot bind the @packshot image column; the copy binds verbatim (no rewriting).

outputs.name: catalog_packshots_x8
outputs.spec: Eight capsule packshots (MF-01..MF-08), each neutralized to its in-frame grey card and matched to ONE shared white point and brightness across the whole batch under one authored brushed-steel house look, with each bare-stainless piece reading true neutral steel and each plated piece holding its genuine colourway, then each piece isolated onto ONE shared solid catalog ground (soft neutral light-grey, e.g. #E9E9E9) via image_remove_background with a backgroundColor — the grey card and sweep gone, metal edges clean with no halo, and every interior gap (bail loops, chain-link holes, ring centre) reading as clean ground because each piece was shot on the same light-grey sweep the ground matches. Delivered as the isolated packshots (grey card cropped/knocked OUT) alongside their RETAINED pre-crop neutralized masters (the *_neutral full-res frames, grey card still in frame) which the harness keeps as the neutrality-grading artifacts. sRGB PNG, long edge ~2048 px and >=300 DPI at the US Letter review-sheet image frame. Acceptance (grader-checked, two SEPARATE claims): (a) neutralisation is graded on the RETAINED pre-crop neutralized master of each frame (its 18% grey card still present) — the card region reads a clean neutral (per-channel spread within a hair of zero) with the whole set matched to one shared white point, stainless true neutral and plated true to colour, no channel clipped to 0 or 255; (b) card-exclusion and interior-gap integrity are checked separately on each delivered isolated packshot (no card pixels present; bail/link/ring interiors read as the shared ground, not solid-bricked). The neutrality tolerance is never evaluated on the card-excluded packshot. Accompanied by a report of the final white-balance (temperature/tint) and exposure move applied to each frame. DELIVERABLE 1.

outputs.name: pendant_spec_lineart.svg
outputs.spec: Clean factory-ready vector SVG of the compass pendant technical drawing, traced ONLY after the flat 2D sketch is straightened (its ~4deg skew removed) and tight-cropped to the mark (paper margin dropped) — crisp at any print size for the manufacturing spec, with no captured paper grain or skew. Produced from the flat raster drawing, NOT from any photograph of the finished piece. DELIVERABLE 2.

outputs.name: variant_rosegold_antique_bronze.jpg
outputs.spec: Authored seasonal colourway variant of the MF-04 rose-gold pendant: the plating deepened to a rich, slightly muted 'antique bronze' via a masked, luminosity-preserving image_adjust_hsl pass pair (a small within-family hue nudge toward bronze plus a saturation/luminance drop that darkens and mutes the warm metal — an in-band adjacent shift, well under a near-complementary rotation) riding the pendant's existing luminosity so its brushed grain, sheen highlights and cast shadow stay natural, touching only the pendant and never the shared ground — no whole-image overlay, no flat fill. Isolated onto the same shared catalog ground as the set. sRGB JPEG. DELIVERABLE 3.

outputs.name: meridian_review_sheets_perSKU.pdf
outputs.spec: Exactly eight press-ready US Letter (8.5x11) portrait product review sheets — ONE single-record sheet per roster row (page-count = row-count = 8) — exported from the one-file-per-row InDesign data-merge; each sheet binds its product_name/sku/material/finish/review_notes verbatim from the roster with its matching grey-card-neutralized isolated packshot dropped into the product image frame via @packshot (a merge bind, never free-form placement); ~300 DPI print quality. document_render_layout exports the WHOLE merged multi-page document in one call (no per-record named export); the review binder is the full eight-page set, one page per SKU. DELIVERABLE 4.

connector_workflow.inputs_from: MF01_compass_pendant_flatlay.jpg, MF02_box_link_chain_flatlay.jpg, MF03_signet_ring_flatlay.jpg, MF04_rosegold_meridian_pendant_flatlay.jpg, MF05_cuff_bracelet_flatlay.jpg, MF06_cufflinks_pair_flatlay.jpg, MF07_onyx_anodized_pendant_flatlay.jpg, MF08_dogtag_compass_pendant_flatlay.jpg, compass_pendant_technical_sketch.png, meridian_reviewsheet_template.indd, meridian_capsule_roster.csv
connector_workflow.note: Load the eight capsule photos, the flat technical sketch, the authored review-sheet .indd template and the SKU roster CSV into the working project in one batch so every downstream step runs against real asset references. Single upload — plumbing, not the difficulty.
MF-01 arrived tilted, so level it before grading and isolation. Only the tilted frames are straightened; deciding which frames need it is part of the job.

MF-01: neutralize this frame to its in-frame 18% grey card and the shared set white point, reasoning the temperature/tint/exposure THIS frame needs from its own card rather than reusing another frame's numbers, then lay the shared brushed-steel house look built from primitives (restrained contrast and clarity to hold the brushed grain, highlights held so the steel does not clip). Authored from primitives, not a preset or auto-tone. Report the final move. Retained as the card-bearing neutrality-grading master.

Isolate MF-01 onto the shared solid catalog ground via remove_background with backgroundColor set to the soft neutral light-grey (e.g. #E9E9E9). This is the connector-legal way to place a subject on a solid ground; the naive select_by_prompt -> invert_selection -> image_fill_area chain is deliberately AVOIDED (it solid-fills a flat plate, bricks the enclosed bail-loop gap and destroys the metal edge). Because the piece was shot on the matching light-grey sweep, the enclosed bail interior retains sweep pixels that read as the ground, and the grey card (a separate object on the sweep) is removed with the background.

Reframe/resize the isolated MF-01 to the shared packshot spec (long edge ~2048 px, sRGB, >=300 DPI at the review-sheet frame), centred with clean margins. onSubjectClipping='extract', downscale-only, never canvas-extend or upscale. Feeds catalog_packshots_x8 and the @packshot cell for MF-01.

MF-02: neutralize this frame to its own grey card and the shared white point, reasoning its own temperature/tint/exposure delta (its correction sign differs from the cool-session frames), then apply the shared brushed-steel house-look constants; protect the highlights on the polished link facets. Report the move. Retained as this frame's neutrality-grading master.

Isolate MF-02 onto the shared catalog ground via remove_background({backgroundColor:#E9E9E9}). The chain's many enclosed link holes retain the matching light-grey sweep and read as the ground after the outer-background knockout (the tool isolates the outer background only and cannot punch enclosed holes; the sweep=ground choice is what keeps the link interiors clean). Same anti-pattern avoidance as MF-01.
Reframe/resize MF-02 to the shared packshot spec. onSubjectClipping='extract', downscale-only. Feeds the set and the @packshot cell for MF-02.
MF-03 arrived tilted, so level it before grading and isolation.

MF-03: its card is close to neutral, so land it on the shared white point with only the small white-balance nudge its own card calls for while making exposure the dominant move (lift toward the set brightness, hold the black point). Apply the shared house-look constants. Report the move. Retained as this frame's neutrality-grading master.
Isolate MF-03 onto the shared catalog ground via remove_background({backgroundColor:#E9E9E9}); the ring's enclosed centre retains the matching sweep and reads as the ground.
Reframe/resize MF-03 to the shared packshot spec. onSubjectClipping='extract', downscale-only. Feeds the set and the @packshot cell for MF-03.

MF-04: read THIS frame's grey card and set only the exposure/brightness needed to match the set, holding white balance to whatever its own already-neutral card requires so the piece keeps its genuine warm plated colourway (the true-to-product bar) rather than being driven to a steel neutral. Apply the shared house-look constants without desaturating the finish. Report the move. Retained as this frame's neutrality-grading master AND the base for the colourway variant.
Isolate the true-colour MF-04 onto the shared catalog ground via remove_background({backgroundColor:#E9E9E9}); enclosed bail loop retains the matching sweep and reads as the ground.

Reframe/resize MF-04 to the shared packshot spec (the true rose-gold packshot that binds into the Meridian Rose-Gold Pendant sheet). onSubjectClipping='extract', downscale-only. Feeds the set and the @packshot cell for MF-04.

MF-05: neutralize this frame to its grey card and the shared white point using the tint axis its own card calls for (the fix here is a green/magenta tint move, not a temperature move), then apply the shared house-look constants. Report the move. Retained as this frame's neutrality-grading master.
Isolate MF-05 onto the shared catalog ground via remove_background({backgroundColor:#E9E9E9}); the cuff's open inner curve is removed with the outer background.
Reframe/resize MF-05 to the shared packshot spec. onSubjectClipping='extract', downscale-only. Feeds the set and the @packshot cell for MF-05.

MF-06: neutralize this split-cast frame to its grey card and the shared white point by balancing temperature AND tint toward the card's neutral, accepting the compromise its two-sided lighting forces rather than fully killing one side, then apply the shared house-look constants. Report the move. Retained as this frame's neutrality-grading master.
Isolate MF-06 onto the shared catalog ground via remove_background({backgroundColor:#E9E9E9}); the isolation spans both cufflinks as the foreground.
Reframe/resize MF-06 to the shared packshot spec. onSubjectClipping='extract', downscale-only. Feeds the set and the @packshot cell for MF-06.

MF-07: neutralize this dark under-exposed frame to its grey card and the shared white point and lift exposure to the set brightness while holding the black point so the anodized surface stays a deep true black — neither crushed to 0 nor washed to grey. Apply the shared house-look constants. Report the move. Retained as this frame's neutrality-grading master.
Isolate MF-07 onto the shared catalog ground via remove_background({backgroundColor:#E9E9E9}); its dark edge cuts cleanly against the light ground, and the enclosed bail retains the matching sweep.

difficulty_rationale: Long-horizon flagship rebuilt from the amputated pendant-plus-chain version: 37 connector calls, 11 distinct Adobe tools, one batch upload fanning into eight dependent per-SKU grade chains plus a variant branch, a vectorize branch, and a genuine composed endpoint (an authored-.indd one-file-per-row data-merge). Difficulty is DEPTH, not repetition: the eight neutralizations are NOT one recipe run eight times — each is a per-frame white-balance/tint/exposure delta reasoned from that frame's own in-frame grey card, whose correction SIGN and AXIS differ (cool-session frames warmed, warm-session frames cooled, a green fluorescent frame corrected on the tint axis not temperature, a split-cast frame balanced to a compromise, an under-exposed dark frame lifted while holding its black point, a genuinely-warm plated frame held), so the naive move of one shared correction visibly fails the match. Layered on that: an agent-authored brushed-steel house look built from image_apply_adjustments primitives (not a preset, not auto-tone); a true-to-product decision that keeps bare stainless neutral while the plated piece keeps its real colourway; a masked luminosity-preserving within-family recolour (rose-gold -> antique bronze) via image_adjust_hsl, the only masked recolour path (color_overlay and fill_area both wrong); a triage between the flat raster sketch (vectorized) and a photographed engraved piece that superficially resembles it (graded and isolated, never traced); prep-before-trace vectorize discipline (straighten -> crop-to-bounds -> vectorize); and the connector-legal isolation via remove_background({backgroundColor}) onto a light ground whose colour matches the shooting sweep so enclosed interior gaps (bail loops, chain links, ring centre) read as ground rather than being solid-bricked. The endpoint is a real merge with an @-image column (text-only vector merge and PDF-converted .indd both fail to bind), gated on page-count == row-count == 8 at >=300 DPI. All steps are headless [C] connector actions; no generative fill/expand, no compositing, no upscaling, no 3D/CAD, no layout-by-coordinates.
hardness_rationale: FAILURE GATE (trippable by a wrong DECISION, not a self-measurement): three gates. (1) Every frame carries an in-frame 18% grey card and the acceptance test is that each card — graded on its RETAINED pre-crop neutralized master (the *_neutral frame, card still present) — reads a clean neutral (per-channel spread within a hair of zero) with the whole set matched to ONE shared white point, and the agent must REPORT the per-frame temperature/tint/exposure it applied; an agent that copies one correction across the batch leaves the cool frames blue, the warm frames orange and the green frame green, and fails. Baked into this gate is a true-colour TRAP: one piece is a genuinely warm rose-gold plated pendant shot under near-neutral light so its card is ALREADY neutral — the naive path applies the same cooling used on the warm-session frames (or 'corrects an imagined warm cast') and strips the real plating colour the client is selling; the correct path reads THAT card and holds white balance. (2) A medium TRIAGE: the flat 2D technical sketch must be vectorized while a photographed engraved dog-tag pendant that superficially resembles line art must be graded and isolated like the other photos — route the photo to vectorize and it returns a muddy silhouette, not a spec; the error is invisible until the file is inspected. (3) The merged deliverable must have page-count == roster-row-count == 8 with each packshot placed at >=300 DPI. HUMAN-HARD ELEMENTS: (a) cross-asset consistency to a measurable target across eight frames shot under two mismatched sessions on differing correction axes (temperature vs green/magenta tint vs split-cast compromise vs tonal-only), which a novice cannot match by eye; (b) constraint-reasoning around tool limits — isolation via remove_background({backgroundColor}) not the select->invert->fill_area plate chain (which bricks the enclosed bail/link/ring gaps and destroys the metal edge), the light ground colour chosen to match the shooting sweep so enclosed interiors read as ground (the tool cannot punch an enclosed hole), masked recolour via image_adjust_hsl (the only masked path, kept within the warm family under a near-complementary rotation) not whole-image color_overlay or flat fill_area, image placement only via a genuine @-image-column .indd merge; (c) prep-before-trace discipline on the skewed, margin-padded sketch. MEASURABLE ACCEPTANCE (decoupled so no artifact is graded on a region it crops away): (a) grey card neutral (channel spread near zero) and one shared white point, evaluated on all eight RETAINED pre-crop neutralized masters (card in frame), stainless true neutral and plated true to colour, no channel clipped to 0/255; (b) card-exclusion and interior-gap integrity checked separately on the eight isolated packshots (no card pixels; bail/link/ring interiors read as the shared ground, not solid-bricked); the antique-bronze variant recoloured within its mask only with sheen and shadow intact; the sketch a clean skew-free vector traced from the drawing not a photo; and exactly one press-ready ~300 DPI US Letter sheet per roster row — plus the reported per-frame WB/exposure params so 'matched' is verifiable rather than asserted.
